reasons: Direction is correct: The Deerskin Companies, Inc. ('Company') is our party (Customer-side alias), and Section 6.1 binds the Company, so the covenant is a restriction on us — a genuine NONCOMPETE deviation. The parallel covenant on HDI in 6.3 was correctly left alone.

Deviation is real and material: the clause sweeps beyond Deerskin Products to 'products substantially similar' and products of unnamed 'companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled', an undefined field-of-use scope with no carve-outs, contrary to the preferred position.

Redline reaches the stated fallback: scope narrowed to the named subject matter (a self-contained 'Deerskin'-branded consumer web site), expressly term-only, with carve-outs for other channels, product development/sourcing and acquisitions; HDI's exclusive brand right is preserved, so the edit is surgical in substance even though textually extensive.

The failed 'minimal edit' check (ratio 0.847) is acceptable here: converting an open-ended field-of-use covenant into the narrowed fallback with carve-outs necessarily requires rewriting the operative sentence; the retained HDI exclusivity clause shows the rewrite was not indiscriminate.
Comment is accurate, appropriately prefixed, states the preferred position (deletion) and the fallback taken, and cites the specific offending language without lecturing.

Minor drafting nit for the negotiator (not disqualifying): carve-out (ii) 'developing, sourcing, marketing or selling any products' is broad enough to be read as swallowing the retained prohibition; tightening it to internal development, sourcing and acquisitions would avoid an internal-inconsistency argument from HDI.
